text: Terminal upgrades for DeepSeek Harness 是一款面向 DSH Web 终端的界面增强插件。它读取 xterm DOM 渲染出的终端行，在按住配置的 Alt、Meta 或 Ctrl 键时识别 HTTP(S) 链接并显示下划线；点击链接会在新浏览器标签页打开目标地址。插件通过 Host 配置路由向浏览器端提供触发键设置，并保留普通点击的终端行为。适合经常从命令输出中打开本地开发服务或网页链接的用户。无需 API 密钥或外部账号。

Terminal upgrades adds link shortcuts to the DSH web terminal. It detects HTTP(S) URLs in xterm rows and underlines them while Alt, Meta, or Ctrl is held. Clicking a link opens it in a new tab; ordinary clicks keep their terminal behavior. No API key or external account is needed.
想在 DSH 终端输出里按住快捷键后直接打开网页链接？
Can I open a URL printed in the DSH terminal with a modifier click?
I want terminal links to underline when I hold a configurable key.
Terminal upgrades 的链接悬停提示：按住配置的修饰键并将指针移到终端 URL 上，插件会识别链接、绘制下划线并显示指针提示；仅支持终端当前可见行中的 HTTP(S) 地址。
Terminal upgrades 的修饰键打开链接：在终端 URL 上按住已配置的 Alt、Meta 或 Ctrl 键并点击，插件会在新浏览器标签页打开该地址；未按触发键时点击仍由终端处理。

dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · Terminal upgrades for DeepSeek Harness：Terminal upgrades for DeepSeek Harness. The first one: hold **Option** over a URL in a terminal and it underlines; click it and it opens in your browser. The trigger key is configurable.

dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · Features：- **The link underlines while you hold the trigger key.** The underline is drawn over the URL's cells in the URL's own color, and the pointer becomes a hand, so you can see what is clickable before you click.
- **Click opens the browser.** Clicking `http://localhost:3000` from `next dev` opens it in a new tab; the desktop app hands the URL to your default browser.
- **Configurable trigger key.** Option by default; Command or Control from the plugin config.
- **Plain clicks are untouched.** Text selection, double-click word selection, and keystrokes reach the terminal exactly as before. Only the trigger key on a link is intercepted.
- **No terminal changes.** The plugin reads the rows the terminal already renders and adds its own overlay; it never rewrites terminal text, so output, colors, and the shell are unaffected.
- **Works with every terminal tab**, including ones opened after installing, and disposes cleanly when the plugin is removed.

dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · Install：In the desktop app, open **Plugins** in the sidebar, choose **Add plugin**, and enter this directory. The desktop profile is managed by the Electron app, which is why this is the preferred path there.

For another profile, use the CLI:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jeremytenjo/dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades.git
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add ./dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades
```

dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · Install：Replace `<profile>` with the name shown by `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config` (for example `web`). Restart the Host or reload the page after installing.

The package ships its browser bundle (`client.js`), so no build step is required to install it.

dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · Usage：1. Run something that prints a URL, for example `pnpm dev` in a Next.js project.
2. Hold the trigger key — **Option** (`⌥`) by default — and move the pointer over the URL. The URL underlines and the terminal cursor becomes a hand. Pressing the key while already resting on a link underlines it without moving the pointer.
3. Click. The URL opens in a new browser tab. In the desktop app it opens in the system browser.
dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · Usage：Without the trigger key, clicking the same URL does what it always did: it places the terminal cursor and starts a text selection.

dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · Configuration：The trigger key defaults to **Option** (Alt). Change it in the plugin's profile entry config:

```yaml

dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml：- id: dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades
  name: "dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades"
  config:
    triggerKey: meta
```

| `triggerKey` | Key |
| --- | --- |
| `alt` (default) | Option on macOS, Alt on Windows and Linux |
| `meta` | Command |
| `ctrl` | Control |

dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml：Restart DeepSeek Harness after changing it: the profile applies plugin config at startup. The Host validates the value while it starts, so an unknown key stops the plugin with an explicit error instead of silently falling back. The browser reads the setting once as the page loads and keeps Option until the answer arrives.

Only the configured key triggers the underline and the click; the other modifiers stay inert, so nothing changes for people who use them for other terminal gestures.

dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · How it works：DeepSeek Harness renders terminals with xterm's DOM renderer, so the visible rows exist as text in the page. The plugin listens on `document`, maps a pointer position to the terminal row and character offset, and runs the same URL rules for any row under the pointer:

dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · How it works：- `http://` and `https://` only.
- Sentence punctuation after a URL and an unbalanced closing bracket are left out, so `see https://example.test/docs.` links the URL without the period.
- A balanced closer stays part of the link, so `https://example.test/a_(b)` keeps its `)`.

dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · How it works：Client plugins do not receive profile entry config, so the Host half validates `triggerKey` and publishes it on one loopback route, `/__dsh/terminal-upgrades`; the browser reads it once at startup. The underline itself is an overlay element the plugin owns, positioned from the URL's text runs, so the terminal's own DOM is never modified.

The plugin adds no slot, no terminal state, and no per-terminal setup, so it has nothing to clean up beyond removing its listeners and its overlay.

dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · Limitations：- **One row at a time.** A URL that wraps onto the next terminal row is not detected; short links such as `http://localhost:3000` are unaffected.
- **Underline is an overlay.** It tracks the text runs the terminal rendered. Scrolling hides it until the pointer moves again, and a very unusual font fallback could shift it by a pixel.
- **Programs that capture the mouse.** In a terminal program that reports mouse clicks itself, such as Vim or `less`, a trigger-keyed click on a link is consumed by the plugin; a trigger-keyed click elsewhere still reaches the program.
- **DOM renderer only.** The detection reads the rendered rows. If the terminal switches to a canvas or WebGL renderer, nothing is detected and the plugin does nothing.
- **Not a general link opener.** File paths, line numbers, and bare host names are not links.

dsh-plugin-terminal-upgrades README · Development：```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run build   # regenerates client.js from src/client.js
pnpm test        # URL, offset, host-route and terminal-screen tests
```

`src/client.js` is the browser source, `index.js` is the Host half, and `scripts/build-client.mjs` bundles the browser half into `client.js` wrapped in the Harness module-loader shape. Edit `src/`, run `pnpm run build`, and reload the page.
